subject: Threshold docking & billing bridge for short-term rate lift
messages:
From: Elena Gomez <elena@brightcart.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T08:31:00-08:00
Subject: Request: short-term throughput lift + billing bridge for holiday launch

Hi Naomi,

Quick note from my side — we’re launching a promotional campaign on Dec 15 that will spike inference traffic for two weeks. Our forecasting team projects a 3–4x increase in token volume during peak windows (attached a short forecast).

Can Redwood provide a provisional throughput uplift (short-term quota bump and higher burst headroom) and a temporary billing arrangement so we don’t get hit with a punitive overrun invoice while the campaign stabilizes? Specifically we’re asking for:
- A temporary quota increase for account BRIGHT-4821 that lasts ~14 days and applies across our primary region (us-east).
- A bridge pricing path (provisional rate or credit) for any overrun during that window, with a clear true-up at month-end.

Procurement wants to understand the financial exposure before signing the PO. If you can outline a simple bridge (example: provisional per-token uplift + credit or capped overrun rate) we can get an expedited PO and start the SOW addendum.

Attached: launch_traffic_forecast.xlsx (forecast summary).

Thanks — we’re trying to avoid throttles during the promo.

—Elena
Elena Gomez
Head of Platform, BrightCart
elena@brightcart.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T10:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term throughput lift + billing bridge for holiday launch

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the forecast.

Short answer: yes, we can stand up provisional headroom and a billing bridge. High level proposal (ready to convert into an SOW addendum):

1) Temporary threshold docking (provisional uplift): +80% baseline throughput for 14 days starting Dec 14 00:00 UTC. Auto-throttle only if consumption exceeds the uplift by >150% for sustained 15-minute windows.

2) Bridge billing approach: bill overrun at a provisional blended rate and apply a launch credit to soften impact. At month-end we true-up actual usage and apply credits/adjustments:
   - Provisional overrun rate: committed unit price for the first 25% above commit, then graduated tiers afterward (Ben — I’m cc’ing you to confirm the tiering below).
   - One-time launch credit to offset noise (example: $5k credit).

3) Operational controls: enable burst guardrails and a realtime alert to your infra team; we’ll provide dashboard access and token-level breakdowns.

If that sounds acceptable, Ben can lock in the exact pricing tiers and I’ll circulate a short SOW addendum (30–60 lines) for DocuSign. Also, please confirm the procurement contact we should send the PO/SOW to.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Gomez <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term throughput lift + billing bridge for holiday launch

Thanks Naomi — looping in the pricing specifics. Elena, appreciate the forecast — we can be prescriptive so procurement knows exposure. Proposed pricing addendum (we can bake into SOW v3):

- Temporary uplift: +80% throughput for 14 days (as Naomi outlined).
- One-time launch credit: $5,000 applied to the first invoice covering the uplift window.
- Overrun billing tiers (post-commit true-up at month-end):
  * 0–25% above commit: billed at committed unit price (no premium)
  * 25–100% above commit: billed at committed unit price +15%
  * >100% above commit: billed at committed unit price +30%
- Cap on exposure: we can cap total provisional overrun charges to a delta not exceeding 2x of monthly committed spend (optional — if you want a hard cap we’ll need procurement sign-off).

Operational notes: we’ll enable streaming alerts and a temporary higher throttle threshold (per Naomi). Karthik — please prepare routing so requests in us-east during the uplift use the dedicated headroom pool and fall back to a verified model variant if capacity is constrained.

I attached a draft SOW (BrightCart_SOW_v3.pdf) and a November usage report for context. If you confirm the PO cadence we’ll mark the uplift window and prepare the DocuSign package.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Pricing | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Elena Gomez <elena@brightcart.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term throughput lift + billing bridge for holiday launch

Naomi / Ben — this looks good and reasonable. BrightCart accepts the provisional uplift (+80% for 14 days) and the tiered overrun construct with the $5k launch credit. A couple of requests before we finalize:

1) Please send the SOW addendum and DocuSign link to procurement@brightcart.com; procurement will raise the PO as soon as they see the agreed terms.
2) We’d like the optional cap on exposure enabled; I’ll flag this in the PO (procurement may ask for a final number — if you can propose a cap amount we can expedite approvals).
3) Can we get the realtime dashboard link and alert subscription for our infra team before Dec 14?

Procurement contact: Maya Patel <procurement@brightcart.com>.
